item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. In SCOPe 2.08 the shared heme-binding four-helical-bundle architecture is only the fold node f.21, SUNID 81344, within class f, “Membrane and cell surface proteins and peptides.” The three named groups are three separate sibling superfamilies under that fold: f.21.1, SUNID 81342, “Transmembrane di-heme cytochromes”; f.21.2, SUNID 81343, “Fumarate reductase respiratory complex transmembrane subunits”; and f.21.3, SUNID 103501, “Respiratory nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain.” SCOPe marks homology as implied at each of those superfamily nodes separately, not across their fold parent. Thus the family-level members below them, such as f.21.1.1/f.21.1.2 for formate-dehydrogenase N gamma subunits and cytochrome bc1 cytochrome b, f.21.2.1/f.21.2.2 for FrdC and SdhC/FrdC-SdhD/FrdD transmembrane subunits, and f.21.3.1 for respiratory nitrate reductase 1 gamma chains, may be treated as homologous only within the appropriate f.21.x superfamily unless other evidence is supplied.
